none.name: Complex numbers and i
none.why: No question, choice or explanation mentions an imaginary or complex number.

none.name: Logarithms
none.why: No question uses one. Exponential questions are answered by reading the model, or by graphing it.

none.name: Permutations, combinations and factorials
none.why: No question asks how many ways something can be arranged or chosen. Probability questions divide one count by another, usually from a table.

none.name: Ellipses, hyperbolas, and a parabola’s focus and directrix
none.why: The circle is the only one of these curves in the bank.

none.name: Sine waves, and the laws of sines and cosines
none.why: Every one of the 38 questions that mention sine, cosine or tangent is about a right triangle or a circle.

none.name: The remainder theorem
none.why: No question asks for the remainder when a polynomial is divided.

rare.name: Polynomial division
rare.why: One Hard question asks which expression equals (x² − 2x − 5) ÷ (x − 3). The answer is x + 1 − 2/(x − 3). College Board’s explanation rewrites the top in terms of the bottom, and names long division only as another way.

rare.name: Sequences
rare.why: One Hard question: each term is a fixed multiple of the one before. That is an exponential function, so the exponential lessons cover it.

keep.name: Factors and zeros of a polynomial
keep.why: The factor theorem, the one piece of the remainder theorem the bank uses: if p(a) = 0, then x − a is a factor of p, and the other way round. 7 questions ask about a factor of a polynomial. Two of them give only a table of values or points on the graph, and the factors come straight from the zeros.
